action: With an empty mesh object Cube.007 in Edit Mode (status bar Verts 0/0), opens Add Modifier and picks Mirror from the Generate list.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, solid shading, reference sheet image in viewport and image editor at left
why: Model only half the head and mirror the other half across X.
reader_equivalent: obj.modifiers.new('Mirror','MIRROR'); m.use_axis[0]=True; m.use_clip=True; m.use_mirror_merge=True; m.merge_threshold=0.001

action: In Right Orthographic over the side-view reference, moves single vertices of a vertex chain to trace the face profile from brow to chin.
view: Right Orthographic, Edit Mode, vertex select, reference image behind
why: The profile line is the centre seam of the face; every later strip is extruded off it.
reader_equivalent: bmesh: create verts at (0, y_i, z_i) read from the side reference silhouette and connect them with edges

action: Extrudes the profile chain sideways into a first column of quads covering forehead, eye and cheek, and drags vertices one by one onto the side reference.
why: Start a strip-by-strip poly layout traced over the drawing.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_edge_only on the profile edges, then set vertex coordinates

action: Keeps nudging vertices of the face strip in side view to sit on the eye socket and cheek line.
why: Match the side silhouette of brow, eye and cheek.
reader_equivalent: v.co.y += 0.0048; v.co.z -= 0.0024 for the chosen vertex

action: Switches to Front Orthographic and slides vertices sideways so the half-face strips follow the front reference: a centre column, a band across the eyes and a jaw line to the chin.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, front reference behind
why: Fit the width of the face to the front drawing.
reader_equivalent: set v.co.x of each strip vertex from the front reference outline

action: Checks the face patch from Top Orthographic (it reads as a shallow V) and then refines the eye-region quads in side view.
why: Give the face front-to-back curvature so it is not flat.
reader_equivalent: push vertices back in Y as their |x| grows, e.g. v.co.y += k*abs(v.co.x)

action: In front view, slides vertices along their edges (G G) to even out the grid of loops around the eye area.
why: Spread the quads evenly without changing the silhouette.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.transform.vert_slide(value=0.0495) or move verts by lerp along the edge

action: In Object Mode applies Shade Smooth (Keep Sharp Edges on) to check the forms of the half mask (59 verts, 40 faces with mirror).
why: Read the curvature of the low-poly face.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth(keep_sharp_edges=True)

action: Back in Edit Mode, the centre-line faces below the eyes are pulled forward into a small pointed nose.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, solid with reference behind
why: Anime nose is a small wedge on the centre line.
reader_equivalent: select centre faces under the eyes, bmesh.ops.extrude_face_region, translate +(-Y) forward

action: Extends the centre strip down from the nose to the chin and moves its edge to the mouth line.
why: Give the mouth and chin a centre column.
reader_equivalent: extrude bottom edge of nose strip, translate in -Z

action: Scales the mouth-row vertices and extrudes the mouth-row edge outward to the mouth corner, then merges stray vertices (M) to close the area between mouth and cheek.
why: Build the mouth area from the centre column outward.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.scale; bmesh.ops.extrude_edge_only; bmesh.ops.pointmerge(verts=[a,b], merge_co=b.co)

action: Bevels the selected mouth edges to split the mouth into a ring of loops.
why: A loop around the mouth gives the lips a rim.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.bevel(offset=0.0178, segments=1, affect='EDGES', loop_slide=True)

action: Moves single vertices of the new mouth ring to the drawn lip line; the mouth is a shallow inset slit in the geometry.
why: Shape the mouth opening in geometry.
reader_equivalent: set vertex coordinates of the mouth ring

action: Fills the open holes between mouth ring, cheek and jaw with new faces (F), switching between edge and vertex select.
view: User Orthographic and Right Orthographic, Edit Mode
why: Close the lower face into one surface.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.contextual_create(bm, geom=[border verts/edges])

action: Extrudes the top edge of the face upward over the forehead and rotates/moves it in side view to start the skull.
view: Front Orthographic (X-ray look over reference) then Right Orthographic
why: Grow the head up from the face.
reader_equivalent: extrude top boundary edges, rotate about X, translate

action: Extrudes the side boundary of the face backward as a strip that will become the side and back of the head, behind the cheek.
why: Wrap the mask around into a closed head.
reader_equivalent: extrude rear boundary edges toward +Y and adjust

action: Adds more rows to the back strip and drags its outer vertices to the back-of-head silhouette.
why: Close the skull shape.
reader_equivalent: translate boundary verts to the side silhouette

action: Finishes the back of the head: the head is a closed shell with the face, skull and back strip (123 verts on the half).
why: Complete head volume before joining.
reader_equivalent: n/a (vertex placement)

action: In Object Mode the finished head sits on the body object Cube (Model collection: Cube, Cube.001 to Cube.006, Cube.007); after this the head is part of Cube (Objects count drops from 1/10 to 1/9 and Cube.007 leaves the outliner).
why: Head and body become one mesh so the neck can be bridged.
reader_equivalent: select head and body, body active; bpy.ops.object.join()

action: On the body mesh, adds a loop cut on the neck and slides it to meet the head.
why: Match neck loop count to the head opening.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.loopcut_slide(MESH_OT_loopcut={'number_cuts':1}, TRANSFORM_OT_edge_slide={'value':0})

action: Selects vertices on the head underside and the neck top and fills faces between them (F) one patch at a time.
why: Bridge the head shell into the neck.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.contextual_create(geom=[4 verts]) per gap, or bmesh.ops.bridge_loops on the two rings

action: Uses the Knife (K) to cut a new edge across the neck join where vertex counts differ.
why: Route edge flow between head and neck.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.connect_vert_pair(bm, verts=[a,b])

action: Fills the remaining hole under the jaw (F), undoes one try (Ctrl+Z) and connects vertex pairs (J) to keep quads.
why: Close the neck seam with clean faces.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.contextual_create; bmesh.ops.connect_vert_pair

action: Checks the joined body-and-head from a 3/4 view in Object Mode.
why: Silhouette check of the whole figure.
reader_equivalent: render a viewport screenshot from a 3/4 camera

action: Selects two faces on the side of the head and extrudes them out along their normal to start the ear.
why: Ear is a block extruded from the head, not a separate object.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_face_region on the 2 ear faces, translate along face normal 0.035

action: Shapes the ear block by moving its vertices (pointed elf-like ear in front view).
why: Match the ear outline of the reference.
reader_equivalent: translate ear verts

action: Turns on X-ray/see-through (Z pie) in front view and slides vertices around the eye so loops follow the drawn eye shape.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, mesh see-through over reference
why: Fit eye loops directly over the reference eye.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.transform.vert_slide(value=0.527) or place verts on the traced eye outline

action: The eye area has been opened into a hole (reference visible through it); moves vertices of the opening to the eye outline.
view: Right Orthographic and Front Orthographic, Edit Mode
why: Eye socket opening shaped in geometry.
reader_equivalent: delete the eye faces (bmesh.ops.delete context='FACES'), then position the border verts

action: A cap of faces now fills the eye; adds a loop cut and scales it, giving an eyeball patch with rings.
why: Add rings for the iris and eyelid edge.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.loopcut_slide(...); bmesh.ops.scale

action: Zooms into the eye in see-through front view and Ctrl-clicks to pick a shortest path of vertices around the eye.
view: Front Orthographic, Edit Mode, see-through over reference
why: Select the eye ring loop.
reader_equivalent: bmesh shortest path: select verts by distance to eye outline

action: Selects the ring inside the eye and scales it down to about half to make an iris ring (center fan of verts).
view: Front Orthographic, see-through over reference eye
why: Iris and pupil rings to place the painted eye texture later.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.inset_region or extrude ring + bmesh.ops.scale(vec=(0.51,0.51,0.51), space=center)

action: Selects the whole eye patch with Select Linked (L) in side view.
why: Grab the eye patch as a unit to push it in.
reader_equivalent: flood-fill select faces bounded by seam edges

action: Loop-selects (Alt) the eye ring and pushes it back into the head so the eye sits recessed in a socket.
why: Eye surface lies inside the eyelid rim.
reader_equivalent: translate eye-patch verts +Y (into head) by 0.0026

action: Result checked in 3/4 view: a recessed oval eye with an inner iris ring and a rim around it.
why: Check depth of the socket.
reader_equivalent: viewport capture

action: Shift+Alt loop-selects the upper eyelid edge and extrudes it out over the eye into a thick lash/upper-lid flap.
why: The anime upper lash line is a geometry ridge over the eye.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_edge_only on the upper lid edge loop, translate forward and up

action: Checks the lash flap overhang in side view and in wireframe.
view: Right Orthographic solid, then User Orthographic wireframe
why: Make sure the flap overhangs the eye.
reader_equivalent: viewport capture

action: In see-through front view, extrudes vertices along the drawn eyebrow to start a brow strip.
why: Eyebrow is raised geometry.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_vert_indiv / create verts along the brow line

action: Select Linked (L) on the brow faces and loop-selects a forehead face strip (Shift+Alt) where the brow will sit.
why: Isolate the brow strip.
reader_equivalent: select connected faces

action: Extends the brow strip with Ctrl-click extrude to cursor and moves it forward off the forehead as a thick separate ridge.
why: Brow reads as a raised block above the eye.
reader_equivalent: extrude brow faces and translate along -Y (forward)

action: Adds a small extruded detail under the brow near the eye and a crease edge (purpose not readable).
why: Extra facial detail near the eye.
reader_equivalent: translate selected verts
